Q: Copy uv-installed tool to next stage of Docker build A:

Use uv sync to install into a standard virtual environment (.venv) and make sure your Python interpreter exists in the exact same path in the builder and final stages.

The easiest way is to run uv inside an image identical to your final target. Something like this would work:

FROM gcc:15-trixie AS builder

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y python3 python3-venv

COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:latest /uv /usr/local/bin/uv

WORKDIR /app

COPY . .

RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev

RUN uv pip install .

FROM gcc:15-trixie

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y python3

COPY --from=builder /app/.venv /app/.venv

ENV PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"

CMD ["sandworm"]

Q: Using abstract subclass in Doctrine : curious database generation A:

I recommend the following setup:

/**
 * @ORM\MappedSuperclass
 */
abstract class SuperAbstractClass {...}

and

/**
 * @ORM\MappedSuperclass
 */
abstract class AbstractClass extends SuperAbstractClass {...}

and 

/**
 * @ORM\Table(name="concreteclass1")
 * @ORM\Entity
 */
class ConcreteClass1 extends AbstractClass {...}

This will create only one table in your schema (named concreteclass1) and having all attributes of your Concrete, Abstract and SuperAbstractClass. Still you can use generic functionality (e.g. id generation will work).

If you have an additional ConcreteClass it will create a new table/entity then again inheriting anything you'll need.

We have this setup as well - from my understanding there is no need to have a joined inheritance here.

Q: What are some idiomatic options to provide both mutable and immutable iterators, while avoiding duplication of traversal logic? A:

You could move the logic of the traversal into methods of your "map-like data structure" and then call those methods in the implementation of each iterator, reducing the amount of code in each iterator to a minimum. Implementing Index and IndexMut may help, and would make your implementation more idiomatic. You could also check the implementation of Rust's standard library HashMap.

Q: Reference a sheet with today's date as the name A:

Depending on the date format you can use INDIRECT with TODAY and Text. This works for me...

=indirect("'"&text(today(),"MM/DD/YYYY")&"'!A5")
